summary: Single-recipe filled command button with an inverted background and primary foreground for actions that must remain legible across ordinary surfaces.
useWhen: A command needs the filled button structure with the fixed inverted background treatment.
The action should use primary foreground content on the inverted surface without exposing intent or contrast choices.
A compact, icon-only inverted action needs an explicit accessible name.
The command has closely related alternatives and needs split mode while keeping the same inverted recipe.
avoidWhen: The action needs semantic intent or contrast-specific filled treatments; use ButtonFilled.
The action is unfilled icon-only shell, navigation, overflow, or tool-rail chrome; use ButtonUnfilled.
The element represents navigation rather than a command.
The content is a persistent selected state rather than an action.

alternatives.when: The action's consequence needs a semantic intent or the fill must adapt through contrast.
alternatives.reason: ButtonFilled owns intent and contrast-aware filled command treatments.

alternatives.when: The action is shell, navigation, overflow, or tool-rail chrome.
alternatives.reason: ButtonUnfilled owns unfilled chrome, active state, borders, and surface-aware interaction states.

alternatives.when: The user is choosing a destination in application navigation.
alternatives.reason: PanelNav owns destination selection and navigation semantics.

accessibility: Provide an explicit accessible name for icon-only buttons.
In split mode, provide menuAriaLabel for the appended ChevronDown segment, pass controls with the Menu id, and synchronize expanded with the Menu open state.
Set hasMenu when the action opens a Menu; it implies aria-haspopup of menu and renders the trailing chevron. Pass controls with the Menu id and expanded from the same open state given to Menu.
Use haspopup directly for a non-menu popup such as a dialog; that case gets no chevron.
Loading keeps the action focused and named, exposes busy and disabled state, and blocks activation.
Use native submit behavior for form submission and handle the form submit event rather than submitting from the button click event.
states: Every size applies one complete control-density recipe across frame height, inline padding, icon zone, text-container inset, gap, and radius.
The inverted background and primary foreground are fixed; ButtonInverted has no intent, contrast, parent-surface, or optional-border props.
Every button has a minimum inline size equal to its resolved height. Short labels therefore form a square control while longer labels continue to hug their content.
Set isInset only when the button is nested inside a same-size control. The default single inset removes 4px overall; insetDepth double removes 8px overall and falls back to single at xs.
Rounded changes only the control radius to the half-radius treatment; it does not change the inverted recipe, size, variant, or interaction semantics.
Loading prevents duplicate activation without applying inactive opacity or removing the current keyboard focus.
Icon and icon-label loading replace the icon in place. Label-only loading centers the loader while preserving the button's measured width.
Physical press scaling is on by default. Disable it only when an owning composite must keep child or background geometry fixed; hover and pressed interaction washes remain available.
ButtonInverted has no active, pressed, or selected state; a filled action is a command, not a toggle or persistent selection.
An open popup is a transient pressed state. While surfaceOpen is true the pressed wash is held for the popup's complete rendered lifecycle without introducing selected styling.
Split mode supports label, icon, and icon-label primary segments. The primary segment emits dsClick and the appended menu segment emits dsMenuClick.
responsiveBehavior: Use fill width only when the parent layout calls for a full-width action, commonly on narrow form layouts.
Choose density from the containing layout so the inverted action matches neighboring controls.

customElements: For form submission, use the native submit type and listen to the form submit event; use dsClick for non-submit commands.
react: Keep async state in the owner and pass it to the loading state until the command settles.
angular: Keep async state in the owner and pass it to the loading state until the command settles.

styling.rationale: The component owns the protected recipes below; unspecified host properties and application layout remain customizable.

protected.reason: The control density is one atomic recipe; use the size and inset props instead of replacing internal metrics.
The component owns its corner treatment; select the supported radius treatment.
The button owns hug/fill sizing and its minimum square geometry; use width and constrain the surrounding layout.
The component owns its surface and interaction treatment; use its semantic presentation props or compose an application-owned surrounding surface.
